q: Art 14 protects 'persons' while Arts 15-16 protect 'citizens'. Which rights does a foreign national retain?
a: Only Art 14, plus Arts 20, 21 and 22. Arts 15, 16 and 19 are citizens-only.
tip: Rights-holder test decides half the FR questions. Foreigner in the stem -> kill 15/16/19.

q: CORRECTED: does Art 15(2) require State funding for shops and hotels?
a: NO. 15(2)(a) shops, restaurants, hotels and places of entertainment carry NO funding condition and bind PRIVATE parties. Only 15(2)(b) wells, tanks, ghats and roads need State funds or public dedication.
tip: Horizontal FRs = 15(2), 17, 23, 24. They bind private persons.

q: CORRECTED: what did the AP Reorganisation Act 2014 actually provide about the capital?
a: Hyderabad as COMMON CAPITAL for not more than 10 years, a period that ended 2 June 2024, plus an expert committee (Sivaramakrishnan, Aug 2014). The Act did NOT name Amaravati - that was a 2015 State decision.
tip: Act versus State decision - a source trap.

q: Which Article was written specifically for Andhra Pradesh, and by which amendment?
a: Art 371D, with 371E, inserted by the 32nd Amendment 1973 after the Six-Point Formula. Executed by the AP Presidential Order 1975: local cadres, local candidates, Administrative Tribunal. It survived the 2014 bifurcation and applies to AP and Telangana.
tip: 16(3) = Parliament by LAW. 371D = President by ORDER. Different actors.

q: Preventive detention: is the Advisory Board period 2 months or 3 months?
a: THREE months. The 44th Amendment's 2-month rule, with a SITTING High Court judge as chair, was passed but NEVER brought into force.
tip: Any option saying 2 months is wrong. Enacted is not operative.

q: CORRECTED: what is the Lok Sabha's maximum strength today?
a: 550 = 530 States + 20 UTs. The old figure 552 included 2 Anglo-Indians, ended by the 104th Amendment on 25 Jan 2020. Actual strength 543. Rajya Sabha: 250 maximum (238 + 12), actual 245.
tip: Rebuild from components 530 + 20; never recall the total.

q: CORRECTED: where does the Godavari enter AP, and where is Polavaram?
a: It enters through ALLURI SITHARAMA RAJU district, via the seven mandals transferred from Khammam in 2014. POLAVARAM is in ELURU district after the 4 April 2022 reorganisation - it was in West Godavari.
tip: Every AP district answer must be checked against the 2022 map.

q: Name the Krishna-system structures in AP from upstream to downstream.
a: Srisailam, then Nagarjuna Sagar, then the Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada. On the Godavari: Polavaram and the Dowleswaram (Sir Arthur Cotton) Barrage. On the Penna: Somasila and Gandikota.
tip: Identify by nearest town: Vijayawada = Krishna, Rajahmundry = Godavari, Nellore = Penna.

q: CORRECTED: distinguish the two bodies called Andhra Mahasabha.
a: Andhra Mahasabha of coastal Andhra: BAPATLA, May 1913, presided over by B.N. Sarma. Andhra Maha Sabha of Hyderabad State, i.e. Telangana: JOGIPET, Medak, 1930. Examiners swap them deliberately.
tip: 1913 Bapatla = Madras Presidency. 1930 Jogipet = Hyderabad State.

q: Give the full 1952-56 chain for the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
a: Potti Sriramulu fasts from 19 Oct 1952 and dies 15 Dec 1952. Andhra State formed 1 Oct 1953, capital KURNOOL - India's FIRST linguistic State. SRC under Fazl Ali appointed 1953, reports 1955. Gentlemen's Agreement 1956. AP formed 1 Nov 1956, first CM Neelam Sanjiva Reddy.
tip: 1953 came from a DEATH; 1956 came from a COMMISSION. Never merge them.

q: Distinguish revenue, fiscal and primary deficit.
a: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure minus Revenue Receipts. Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure minus (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts). Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments.
tip: Fiscal deficit is a FLOW in one year; public debt is a STOCK. Never equate them.

q: Which economic bodies are constitutional and which are not?
a: CONSTITUTIONAL: Finance Commission (280), GST Council (279A), ECI (324), SEC (243K), CAG (148), NCBC (338B). EXECUTIVE: NITI Aayog (Cabinet resolution 2015) and the old Planning Commission (1950). STATUTORY: NHRC, CVC, Lokpal.
tip: 16th Finance Commission - Arvind Panagariya, award period 2026-31.

q: BNS 2023: date in force, section count, and the new offences.
a: In force 1 JULY 2024. 358 sections. New: s.111 organised crime, s.112 petty organised crime, s.113 terrorist act, s.103(2) mob lynching, s.106(2) hit-and-run, s.152 replacing sedition. Community service added as a punishment.
tip: Nyaya = justice = offences = replaces the IPC.

q: BNSS 2023: what changed for an investigating officer?
a: In force 1 July 2024, 531 sections. Zero FIR regardless of jurisdiction (s.173); e-FIR; MANDATORY forensic visit with videography for offences punishable with 7 years or more (s.176(3)); 90-day progress update to the informant; s.187 police custody restructured; trial in absentia for proclaimed offenders.
tip: Suraksha = protection = procedure = replaces the CrPC.

q: BSA 2023: what is the core change?
a: In force 1 July 2024, 170 sections. Electronic and digital records are placed on the same footing as documentary evidence, with an expanded definition covering semiconductor memory and communication devices.
tip: Sakshya = evidence. Translate the middle word and the matching is automatic.

q: CORRECTED: how many Fundamental Duties, and added by which amendments?
a: ELEVEN. The 42nd (1976) gave TEN, on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice. The 86th (2002) added the ELEVENTH, 51A(k), the parent's duty for a child aged 6-14.
tip: 42nd = 10, 86th = +1. Never say the 42nd gave 11.

q: Vitamin deficiency mapping.
a: A - night blindness and xerophthalmia; B1 - beriberi; B3 - pellagra; B12 - pernicious anaemia; C - scurvy; D - rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults; K - impaired clotting.
tip: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and stored; B and C are water-soluble and need daily intake.

q: Common chemical names.
a: Washing soda Na2CO3.10H2O; baking soda NaHCO3; bleaching powder Ca(OCl)Cl; plaster of Paris CaSO4 with half a water; gypsum CaSO4 with two waters; quicklime CaO; slaked lime Ca(OH)2.
tip: Plaster of Paris and gypsum differ only in water of crystallisation - the usual trap.

q: How should an AP scheme be memorised for the exam?
a: Always as name + beneficiary + benefit + department. Thalliki Vandanam is AP's school-education assistance scheme paid to mothers, replacing the earlier Amma Vodi. Verify the current amount from a recent source before the exam.
tip: Scheme names change with governments; the BENEFICIARY and DEPARTMENT rarely do.

q: AP districts and local bodies.
a: 26 districts since 4 APRIL 2022, up from 13. Tiers: Gram Panchayat, MANDAL Parishad, Zilla Parishad. Sarpanch, MPTC and ZPTC are DIRECTLY elected; MPP and ZP Chairperson INDIRECTLY. AP gives 50% women's reservation by State law. AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994.
tip: The constitutional floor is one-third; AP's 50% comes from STATE law.

q: The 1919 cluster.
a: Rowlatt Act March 1919; Jallianwala Bagh 13 April 1919 at Amritsar; the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and the Government of India Act 1919 introducing DYARCHY in the provinces; the Hunter Committee inquiry; Tagore renounced his knighthood.
tip: One year, several events. Exams ask which does NOT belong to 1919.

q: CORRECTED: AP's soils.
a: RED soils cover about two-thirds - Rayalaseema and the uplands - suited to groundnut and millets. BLACK regur in parts of Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Prakasam and Guntur - cotton. DELTAIC ALLUVIAL in the Godavari-Krishna deltas - the RICE BOWL and the most exam-relevant soil. Also coastal sands and laterite.
tip: The original card omitted deltaic alluvium, AP's most important soil.

q: Emergency provisions at a glance.
a: 352 National - war, external aggression, armed rebellion; approval in 1 month by SPECIAL majority; used 1962, 1971, 1975. 356 President's Rule - 2 months, SIMPLE majority, maximum 3 years; beyond 1 year needs an Emergency in force plus an EC certificate. 360 Financial - NEVER used.
tip: The harder emergency has the shorter clock: 352 one month, 356 two.

q: ISRO and the AP connection.
a: ISRO headquarters Bengaluru. Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, SRIHARIKOTA, is in TIRUPATI district after 2022 - previously Nellore - adjoining Pulicat Lake, India's second-largest brackish-water lagoon.
tip: SHAR is in AP and is asked directly. Note the post-2022 district.

q: CORRECTED: literacy, Census 2011.
a: INDIA 72.98%, about 73% - NOT 74%. Undivided AP 67.02%, the lowest among the major States. Residuary AP about 67.4%. Kerala highest, Bihar lowest.
tip: Always quote 72.98 for India. The 74% figure in the old card was wrong.

q: GST rests on which Articles?
a: THREE. Art 246A is the concurrent taxing power and the actual charging provision; Art 269A covers inter-State supply and IGST; Art 279A creates the GST Council. 101st Amendment 2016. Council voting: Centre one-third, States two-thirds, decisions by a three-fourths majority, quorum one-half.
tip: Most notes give only 279A. 246A is the power; 279A is the body.

q: The Satavahanas, in exam detail.
a: Founder SIMUKA. Principal capital PRATISHTHANA, that is Paithan; the later seat was DHANYAKATAKA or AMARAVATI. Greatest ruler GAUTAMIPUTRA SATAKARNI, known from the NASIK inscription of his mother Gautami Balashri. Amaravati's fame is the MAHACHAITYA, a Buddhist stupa.
tip: Ancient Amaravati, the stupa, and modern Amaravati, the capital, are the same site.

q: AP river and coast superlatives.
a: The Godavari is the longest river in AP and the longest in PENINSULAR India, rising at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik. AP's coastline is about 974 km - SECOND longest among the States, after GUJARAT. Highest peak: Arma Konda in the Eastern Ghats.
tip: Superlatives are asked one rank off. Gujarat, then AP, then Tamil Nadu.

q: Ombudsman and anti-corruption bodies.
a: Lokpal at the Centre and Lokayukta in the States under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - STATUTORY, not constitutional. AP has its own Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act 1983. The CVC is statutory (2003); the CBI operates under the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act 1946.
tip: None of these is constitutional. The CAG and the ECI are.

q: Atmospheric layers and the ozone question.
a: Troposphere - weather, temperature falls with height. STRATOSPHERE - the OZONE layer, temperature rises with height. Mesosphere - meteors burn up. Thermosphere with the ionosphere - radio reflection. Exosphere - outermost.
tip: Ozone is a POLLUTANT in the troposphere and a SHIELD in the stratosphere.
